newsitem.title: GERMANY: SPD's Schroeder still sceptical of EMU start date.
newsitem.headline: SPD's Schroeder still sceptical of EMU start date.

text.p: Gerhard Schroeder, a leading potential candidate for chancellor for the opposition Social Democrats (SPD), said on Tuesday he remains sceptical of the scheduled January 1999 start for European monetary union.

Schroeder, state premier of Lower Saxony, said at a banking conference too little progress had been made on common European economic, finance and social policies for the planned start date to make sense.
He called for a rational debate on the issue, and advised against a purely technical discussion of the 1999 start date, the BVR banking association said in a summary of the proceedings.
"It is much more important that actual harmonisation take place in these areas," BVR quoted him as saying.
The hope that the single currency would create masses of new jobs in Germany is "dangerous economic nonsense," he said.
On the contrary, in the near term it will increase pressure on the labour market, he said.
The stability criteria must be applied strictly and without creative bookkeeping, he said.

Public opinion polls indicate Schroeder would beat Chancellor Helmut Kohl if elections scheduled for 1998 were held today, but it is far from certain he will beat SPD leader Oskar Lafontaine as the party's candidate.
Kohl is commited to the January 1999 start date for EMU.
